comment: Very well maintained, easy hike with beautiful trees and rock formations.

Buy parking ahead of time - it’s an online reservation portal and we didn’t have service so we had to double back to a place with service to get our reservation. Once we were in it was awesome! Great views, very obvious signage, and a fun hike!
A little short, but beautiful views and many options for trails

A nice walk along a cliff. There are views of farmland and a few mansions. 

For this trail follow the directions on All Trails. Don’t go to the main entrance.
It’s well maintained, well marked trail. Multiple viewpoints, shaded. Will be back!!
Wonderful loop for a morning hike especially on hot days as it is mostly covered by trees and provides a nice amount of shade while not feeling to cold.
super fun with great views and sitting spots to enjoy!! would definitely recommend and come back to! :)
Trail is well marked and maintained. Completely dry. Mozzies were there but not bad. Easy but also good amount of mini climbs and descents. Super dog friendly. Great trail!!
Good. But expensive
Lovely shaded trail
Lots of poison ivy but beautiful views!

Found some garbage here and there but wasn't much of an issue as there are garbage cans at the trail head/ middle. Very well maintained and marked trail. All kinds of terrain, gravel, roots, rocky, smooth. Downside is very touristy trail, some speakers here and there. But overall favorite trail in ontario so far. Really the worst thing about it is it's not longer.
The quarry is where the cliffs are to rock climb. Fun caves to explore too
Great time to see the trilliums, there are literally thousands of them out
Amazing views along the whole trail!

I made the decision to start from the other entrance which was a bit of a mistake as it doesn’t make the full loop. If you’re doing this trail then definitely start from bruce trail parking lot and it’ll make things a lot easier.
Went with my dog and we both had a great time :)
Beautiful trail with some beautiful views
Soft but not muddy. Great hiking conditions.
Found a tick on me after this trail be careful
The rating had nothing to do with the trail itself. I just came too close to slipping many times in the very wet conditions. I turned back. I'll definitely return in drier times.
Nice short local hike! Conditions were great, although it is a very busy trail! Can see views all the way to the CN Tower!
Always love coming to Nemo
Nice easy trail! Cliffs and those open caves are really cool!
Can be a bit of a climb at first but well worth it.
Directions posted were easy to follow and the view is amazing!

Part nine of our Bruce Trail at Uruguay section, some road walking some scrambles we detoured a couple of times the weather was crazy, but of course we loved it, Robin‘s now and turkey vultures cows along the way and horses

Such a great trail - a bit of a climb up the escarpment but then was level and great. Beautiful views. Can appreciate it would be really muddy if it wasn’t frozen today! For dog owners - there is a little ladder, our dog is only medium so we could lift her but I could imagine it would be hard with a bigger doggo!
Sooo nice lots of uphill climbing & a ladder
Beautiful day, beautiful views. Icy in parts and slushy in others. Crampons would of been useful (especially icy parts near cliff edge, but easily navigable).
Great views especially during winter. Enjoyed the uphill-downhill action at both ends of the trail.
It was a lovely day
Extremely icy conditions, treacherous in parts.
102.6km to 82.6km

First off, the entry to this is quite hard and pretty dangerous when slippery. Very steep path that requires climbing on and over rocks with no handholds. If you're not prepared for that, don't go.  Once up that though, the trail on the top of the escarpment is beautiful and well maintained and easy enough to walk around.
Beautiful fall views, no bugs this time of year, and not a lot of people on a week day.

October 26, 2025. 
Great hike, great colors. Was very very crowded. We did Rattlesnake and Mount Nemo today. Rattlesnake is probably has more beautiful views to my opinion. Theres 2 toilets, one right at the entrance - porta potty, and the second is metal round shape toilet at the beginning of the trail which door does close so you need second person to hold the door shut for you. They don't charge you for parking, but entrance is 11$ for adult person. 
We hiked in Quebec and Banff, there's only few places that charge you for parking like lake Louse. what's the reason when you wanna hike in Ontario - government drain money from you just do to recreational activities?  
Kelso, Crawford, Rattlesnake, Mount Nemo are all in close proximity. Why do I need to pay 24$ for 2 people every time I enter one of those?
Lots of open cliffs, beware for children!
Chill and nice walk
It is a nice walk but 30 dolars (2 people) for it is insane. Easy, but just nothing so special.

Trail was very pretty with great views. Some rocky bits were slippery due to wear from people walking over them. Clearly marked, no bugs, sporadic fall coulours were beautiful. It's just one steeper climbing section that takes time, but nothing difficult. Would be harded if conditions were icy, wet, or muddy, so keep an eye out!

This is a nice trail and not very hard. A the start when you need to up the hill you need to be careful and not slip when it’s wet. Take your time and will be fine! 
Very nice view on the Est side. If the sky is clear you can see Toronto on the horizon!
I recommend you to do this trail
Challenging trail.  Lots of rock outcrops to maneuver.  Wear good soles shoes.  Views are amazing.
Lovely end of summer / early fall hike. Just starting to see some fall colours.
Amazing and well marked
My first hike ever :) Moderate due to some of the rocky uphill parts but overall, great experience with great views. Parking was easy.

It was good starting is tuff then easy because it was high in starting then good and then get out of trees shadows face sun heat that was hot then again easy cliffs are wonderful * overall excellent we like it we cook over there we bring portable stove so we eat sandwiches
Very relaxing and breathtaking trail
Cool walk
Good trail, most of the trail is easy with some more challenging areas. The view at the top was nice but seemed to be of the same expensive house for most of the trail.
Very rad

Beautiful rocky
 trail
45 minutes from Brant is this paradise! Barely a soul around, nothing extremely challenging, some jumps need to be made along the path but absolutely must do day hike!

Second time visiting this trail and had a blast, amazing views from the top of the mountain overlooking the whole city, all paths were well maintained and plenty of different terrains to explore. Only complaint was it was very busy and was walking alongside people the whole hike. Other than that, highly recommended - 8.1/10

The South loop trail didn't loop and seemed to lead from MN11 on the map to the parking lot on walkers line, which is not great if you parked at the main entrance lot at the opposite end.  They need to have some signage or early warnings that the loop is no longer a loop.
Mount Nemo, North and South Loop all great views and nice hike
Gorgeous trail, make sure you buy your park entry online before driving there.
Trail is well maintained, beautiful view. Don't need to do the full loop-past mount Nemo point the view is meh. It's better to turn back and still get to see the amazing view on your way down

If you want a short hike then this is for you. It’s not great as a Bruce Trail hike.  First, nothing worse for a hiker than loose gravel trail in full sun. That’s how this starts.  Your first left is a main BT but the map doesn’t indicate the closed part of the trail due to regeneration so you basically do a short loop. The other BT is picked up by the side trail and then loops to main and ends at Walkers Line. Then there is a 5km road walk to pick up again. Forget that. So turned around there too.

Won’t be back to Mt Nemo. I managed 9 km and unless I wanted to do trail repeats, that’s it. 

Some really nice views. A little bit of elevation that is always nice. It was hot out so not too crowded on a Sunday. But great in forest on a 30+ day

Great views, well maintained but rocky areas. Hiking shoes recommended. There are lots of open cliff edges and gaps just off trail so be mindful with pets and kids. You have to prepay for the entry fee online and the cell service is spotty by the gate so order ahead!

Great trail with beautiful views. Some tougher bits with our kiddo (10). Really enjoyable. We took a shortcut and skipped about 1km of the loop. The Guelph line side of the trail wasn’t my favourite - mostly just gravel, no shade and lots of bugs. Everything else was fantastic.

A beautiful, moderate hike along the escarpment. Lots of places to sit and look out towards Mississauga to the east. 

The route is mostly shaded and there was a nice breeze to keep us cool.
Beautiful trek up the Bruce Trail with many overlooks on the way.
Great easy trail
One of my favourite trails. Top 10.   Love hike down the face of escarpment and then back up. Slippery after a rain.

fun hike! the beginning with the rocks was technical and quite a workout, but afterwards the rest of loop is fairly easy. not muddy at all when I went, and the views are plentiful and beautiful.

also, SO many chipmunks and lots of cool spots to watch a close up of the hawks flying by.
Good trail. Good views aswell. Nice elevations. Intermediate trail
Amazing trail to explore, it’s zen
Beautiful trail

Visited 830am sunday morning in June.  Good amount of parking. 
Great weather so the trail was dry. 
Would call it an Easy Plus trail. Some small elevation changes but nothing super strenuous. Where its a little more challenging than an ‘easy’ trail is that the footing involves stepping over rocks & roots (typical bruce trail type of trail) rather than a smooth gravel trail. 
Great walk through the woods & some good lookout viewing locations. Lots of warnings to keep away from the cliff edge other than at designated locations. 
All Trails showed you could do a bit of a bigger loop by following the bruce trail down towards the Walker Line parking lot & cutting back up to join the other trails but there was no access through so had to back track
Cool.

phone died during hike  
Loved this trail!

The whole trail is lush and green after the May rain. Some fun rockier parts where sure footing is needed or hiking poles could be helpful. The Bruce trail section was my favourite. Some nice lookouts.

Beautiful hike! All the trails are well maintained and are in good condition, took about 3hr total to cover the full trail (including side trails, time to enjoy the view and snacks). Plenty of variety of terrains, rocky climbs, thick forested areas and even a little creek. Overall would recommend and can’t wait to be back!

8.1 / 10
Part of the trail was closed and we had to backtrack

My dog and I absolutely loved this hiking trail! From start to finish, everything was perfect. The trail was incredibly clean, which made the walk even more enjoyable. We were especially impressed by how few bugs there were—such a nice surprise for a nature walk!

There were plenty of scenic lookout points along the way, giving us lots of chances to stop, take in the views, and relax. We also saw a number of turkey vultures soaring above, which added to the experience. The trail itself was very well maintained and easy to follow.

Overall, we had a fantastic time and will definitely be coming back. Highly recommend to anyone looking for a peaceful, beautiful, and dog-friendly hike
Stretch!
I was here 3 years ago, and the signage and Trail markers are much improved now. It's marked as easy, but i would classify it closer to moderate. It was a good hike. Nice views
Great conditions. Easy to park. Wish there was a restroom close by.
Not muddy great views
Nice views all through out. On this specific route, the trail for the loop is currently closed towards the Walkers Ln side.
Great hiking trails lots of beautiful views and amazing craves caves
Perfect clear day!

Fantastic spot for hikers seeking scenic beauty. During my visit, I was delighted to spot woodpeckers, adding a special touch to the natural experience. The area's diverse ecosystem makes it a must-visit for anyone who appreciates the outdoors.
60 minutes of barefoot hiking in the woods makes for a happy Marius!

This is a hard hike but so worth the effort the views are incredible. Prepare for steep inclines and thin walkways along the trail edge, there are chains and a ladder to help in some areas. Very wet and muddy (it’s mid march after lors of rain) making rocks very slippery, boots are definitely recommended. This loop is actually 7.5kms so prepare for that! As of now the hours are 8am to 7pm with paid parking! They will ticket cars without paid parking. I will definitely be coming back to do this hike in the summer!

Great views along the ridge. Visited during the snow storm, and the deep snow made it a lot more slow going. Trails are pretty wide, would have been a good spot for snow shoeing! Only issue was the loop part towards the end is completely blocked off right now, and we didn’t see that until we got out there. Would recommend taking the last short cut across if you want to do a true loop, rather than an out and back. Some spots were a bit slick so I was glad I had ice cleats.
Packed snow, not slippery, spikes weren’t needed. Gorgeous day!
Beautiful as always. easy parking, not busy when I went  (snowy Sunday noon). Pack poles and shoe chains, it's icy.
Beautiful trail and views. The hike at the beginning gets your heart pumping but it’s worth it. There’s a small ladder that makes it a little less dog friendly.
With all the snow, there are a couple of slippery spots to watch out for, otherwise a very nice and straightforward trail - even in the winter!
Trail isn’t too busy, decently maintained, entrance isn’t too expensive. Beautiful forest and views. Parts of the AllTrails trail were actually blocked off, however.
A bit muddy from the rain last night. No problem with poles. Very quiet. Only saw 7 people in 2.5 hours.
There’s a step ladder so we had to lift up our 50 pound dog
NOT DOG FRIENDLY. There’s a ladder about 10 minutes into the trail. Beautiful up until that point… we had to turn around!
Beautiful view in the fall.
Easy/moderate trail. Nice views comparable to Dundas Peak. Ensure you have a parking reservation prior to going.
Spectacular views! Fall colors have certainly peaked. Great weather too. Amazing!
Surprisingly crowded on a Monday morning!
Wear good shoes or boots.  Challenging in sections.  Climbing rocks and stepping over roots and other rocks.  Views are amazing.
Absolutely spectacular… no more words needed.
Some very rocky sections.  Wear well fitted footwear. Excellent views.
Amazing trail. Got here super early to watch sun rise.
Great views in Fall.

Says it is dog friendly,  however there is a  ladder which dogs are unable to climb.  Obscene to charge families to walk these trails.  Adults $10.50, child $7.50 plus get.  That's insanely expensive for a family walk.

Great trail to do! Difficult section at the beginning from Walkers line, but manageable. After that the trail is very
good but you need hiking shoes/boots because it is very rocky and lots of roots. Very well marked with a nice lookout point.

Great conditions today, cool but sunny and clear skies. Views off the escarpment are magnificent! If you access the trail at Walkers Line there is a steep climb up some rocks and a wooden ladder. Park at the Guelph Line lot to avoid this. Trail at the top of the escarpment is generally flattened earth and tree roots, with a few scattered crevasses. Highly recommend!
Trail was marked very well. Perfect day for a hike!
No bugs, clear signs so easy navigate. A lot of elevations and a bit challenging. Pretty fun adventure overall!

While the views are nice, it can get crowded, and the noise from the nearby road detracts from the experience. Although the cost is justified by the area’s maintenance, free trails like Old Baldy offer similar or even better views, making it hard to recommend over those options.
Panoramic view of the plains from the mountain ridge was breath-taking.  The path was rocky and you need good shoes. Avoid rainy days as the boulders may get slippery.
Good place for Puff Ball Mushrooms!

lovely cliff edge stuff, scrambly over pitted limestone, easy rises and dips, helpful chain “banister” installed for security along a big, steep rock clamber. some gravelled trails to and from main lookout and also to and from old disused quarry.  

trails are partly white flash BT (and side blue flash BT), and partly Halton Conservation (those trails marked MN for mt. nemo). about 2+ hrs full loop, depending on stoppages for views. absolutely lovely. 

ps. i marked “not crowded” but that’s mid-week. weekends are another matter altogether.

pps: the followong question is about parking capacity. i marked “lots”, but that’s for the guelph line entry point (top of escarpment). lots of parking there. but the walker’s line entry point (below escarpment) has much less capacity. maybe a dozen cars. but that’s not a problem because the route onto the escarpment and mt. nemo from down there goes over a rock fall and there’s a ladder too after that. it’s a proper scramble and thus not to everyone’s taste. many fewer people try this access than the other up top.
Lovely vibes and the view was gorgeous!
Technical spots on trail. Beautiful views, but some bugs
A great hike along the escarpment. No notes! I would rate it moderate because of a couple of scrambles.

Amazing well marked and well maintained trail with beautiful scenery and surroundings 
View from top of Nemo mountain is stunning overlooking Toronto downtown skyscrapers , Mississauga, Brampton and Pearson airport 
Overall worth visiting 
Would go again

Perfect
Moderate trail, good condition with some segments a little on the difficult side due to hazards/obstacles. Otherwise great!

This trail has lot of uphill and downhill. Toronto skyline is visible as a small hazy things. Rough terrain to walk. Could be difficult during monsoon. I walked barefoot cos my shoes was hurting my toes. I got two fresh apples and 
I’m lucky enough to see the sunset
One of my favourite hikes in the region!
Went in the fall, nice hike with some autumn colors. Nothing to write home about.
Beautiful views in multiple points. Make sure to watch your step though.

Some steep parts at the beginning of the trail. There is a small ladder to climb so if you bring your doggo then make sure you can lift them up it! Beautiful views and a cute little hut you can stop to rest or have snacks. I made the mistake of jot bringing bug spray - highly recommend bringing some! I some how missed the  waterfalls which was a bummer but there is a little trail leasing to a quarry (on the map at the entrance of the trail) so perhaps this is where you will want to go for some falls!
Great hike, rough terrain at first until the ladder and just as hard coming down, but great if you’re looking for elevation in the area
Cool trail with stunning lookout views!
Could not get to the route I walked couple of weeks ago due to overgrown plants.
Expect rocks and roots and a bit of climbing, but with fantastic views at the top as your reward!

A great trail albeit the initial part leading on to the main mount is a bit muddy and insect-ridden.

I started this trail at approximately 4pm. The weather was fine. Approximately mid-way through there was light rain which I was shielded from by the canopy.

There is a slightly challenging part of the trail at the beginning which I’ve already alluded to. This difficult terrain consists of a steep rocky incline, including a step ladder. Whilst this is somewhat challenging, it is made more difficult if one is hiking after a downpour because the rocks and ground will be wet and slippery. I would urge caution and a walking stick would come in handy.

Overall, a thoroughly enjoyable hike. I particularly enjoyed the plateau at the pinnacle of Mount Nemo where there is a plethora of cedar trees. This ancient and majestic cedar forest is truly a sight to behold. The sights and sounds of this hik will leave you mesmerised!
so buggy and wet
Ridiculously buggy and slippery

easy, dog friendly trail. end of the trail was closed so we couldn’t loop a portion of it, but overall a very nice trail with lots of lookout points!
Mount Nemo, great hiking trail great views over the cliffs
Great hike! Nice challenging part near the beginning where you need to climb some rocks, great lookout points and contains some quiet and peaceful areas
Probably my favourite location to hike so far. Especially on such a beautiful rainy day.

Nice big parking lot, easy to find a place to park even tho it was a little busy. & for as many cars we saw in the parking lot the trails were very sparse with people! AMAZING views, worth doing all the side trails!
Full loop is not available

Great trail, a little hike. It's peaceful and full of spectacular views. You won't regret it.

Great views all along the escarpment. Excellent condition.

Lovely to be in the woods. Tricky slippery rocks and lots of tree roots to navigate in places.  Gorgeous views of fields, golf courses (people even playing in March!) and the cities beyond.   Thanks Halton Conservation for maintaining the trails so well.
For advanced hikers , don’t go when wet very slippery , not good for bikes,  strollers ,

Trail looks great. But I only managed to do 0.68 km of it ! (At the top of the steep rocks/boulders) there is a ladder. My dog can’t climb ladders… So, if you have a dog and can pick them up, I think you’ll enjoy the trail. Otherwise, learn from my mistake and don’t pay the admission fee and drive over an hour to come here to only be able to walk 0.68 km (one way). Not blaming the trail but didn’t see the ladder listed anywhere on the website or in reviews.

Beautiful colors!
Beautiful views. A variety of different terrains. Challenging but worth the climb.
Awesome hike
Whoa!
Perfect day,no bugs,not muddy,good views. Have to pre pay parking online.

Beautiful trail - especially this time of year.  Perfect weather, perfect views: BUT way too many signs, every 100 steps you will see some type of sign.  These weren’t here 20 years ago.  Anyways, great trail but why so much signage?

Excellent hike with lots of great viewpoints! Would recommend trying all 3 trails so starting from the parking, heading into the south loop and escarpment edge trail, and then finishing off with the north loop trail which will bring you back to the parking. Doing this route is about 8km. Trails are well marked just ensure you follow the white markers along the way. Some sections can be steep and narrow so be cautious and wear proper hiking attire. Went on a Sunday afternoon in October and it wasn’t too busy along the trails as most crowds are around the lookout so you’ll enjoy some quiet time in nature. Note, you’ll need a reservation to enter the park. Overall would recommend!

Beautiful trail, lots  of slick roots and rocks. Went on a windy day and we had shelter along the trail. We followed the trail but we actually covered a distance of 7.98K from the parking lot, not 6.9K. Beautiful views and some cool caves to explore. It was busy on the long weekend but not too crowded. Parking lot is small. There’s a 4 step ladder at the 600m mark and a bathroom around the 5K mark.
Just gorgeous
Some parts rocky. But easy level difficulty.
Very steep trail at beginning
Great trail and spectacular views.
Great location to see autumn leafs!
Trail in good condition, few steep sections at the beginning but enjoyable hike overall.
Rocks and roots!
Well kept. Lots and lots of ankle twisting roots and rocks so watch your step. Great views! Can get busy.
Great trail! Good mixed terrain, make sure to bring bug spray coz we forgot and mosquitos are vicious! There's a small climb on rocks and a 4 step ladder. There's quite a bit of lookouts too!

An awesome trail located just outside of Toronto, this trail offers a comprehensive glimpse into the wonders of Mount Nemo. It treats hikers to breathtaking views of the limestone cliffs, opportunities to explore caves, and a chance to immerse themselves in the area's rich biodiversity.

What surprised me were the light technical climbs and descents at the trail's beginning and end, where you navigate the limestone cliffs. This segment felt reminiscent of "summiting"  mountains and was a standout experience, especially for those longing for a taste of the mountains.

I recommend this trail to anyone seeking an escape to appreciate the natural beauty of southern Ontario. So, stop reading this and get out there!

Great hike! Perfect distance and challenging enough to get a workout in. The beginning and end are quite steep and dangerous so have proper footwear. We didn’t have any issues with bugs but it is also mid September - bring spray just in case. Beautiful views also! Highly recommend.
Great for some bouldering :)
Rocky climb- need good hiking shoes as paths are slippery
the part where there are rocks, becareful.  views are beautiful.   good hike

This is a really nice trail. I brought my two dogs, but I actually wouldn't recommend it for dogs. I'm glad that they're allowed, but it was difficult in some areas. There was a ladder at one point during the hike and I'm a single hiker, so it was hard to get two dogs up a ladder. If you had a bigger dog, I'm not sure if it would be possible. The trail overall is moderate in difficulty and it's located in a really nice area. The drive up was beautiful. That being said, the view from the top was nice, but mostly looking at homes and farmland, so if you're looking for more immersion in nature it might not be the best choice. There are also lots of VERY deep cracks/holes, so if you're a beginner or maybe a little clumsy I would be extra careful. Overall, a lovely hike and I will likely complete it often given its great length, convenient location, and wonderful rocky trail. You also need to reserve parking online in advance!
very easy to get lost - follow trail markers
Not kid friendly , extremely difficult trail, takes an hour to complete, view is not worth it, broke my left leg, wouldn’t recommended to anyone.
Lovely hike!  Mostly in the trees with many views from the escarpment.  Some caution needed on rocky ascent/descent up to the escarpment.  Decent shoes and insect repellent mandatory.

Difficult at first, but gets much easier after the first 1 km. Only washrooms are deep inside the park, so if you’re using this approach then plan accordingly. Mosquitoes and bugs get annoying in the late afternoon, but manageable if you cover all your skin with bug repellent or clothing. Few muddy areas even on dry days but nothing which will mess up clothes or shoes. Lots of photo opportunities along the way so don’t get hung up on the first scenic spot. Overall, great trek with many fun and challenging spots.

moderately challenging for a novice hiker. Your biggest obstacle will be at the beginning of the hike traversing the rock that leads to a small ladder.  It was sketchier on the way down due to the muddy and slippery conditions from rainfall, but, just take your time and be patient... you'll do fine. :)

I found myself off the main trail on multiple occasions, so, be weary of that as well. But, that can be part of the fun when you're just out exploring things for the first time.

It was abit challenging in the beginning but then it wasn’t bad at all absolutely beautiful views a little mud here and there not bad though it started raining when I was almost done so the rocks got a little slippery had my hiking stick with me which was very helpful, a ladder in one area for climbing but not a long one, it is $10.50 admission then it says only 3 hour parking limit on the receipt which was barely enough for me and I didn’t even sit down once just stopped for some photos a couple times.
But all and all a beautiful hike
Absolutely lovely!
Great!  Not easy at the beginning but pretty flat after.
Great morning hike with wonderful views.
Decent hike.
Good knees and hips required for some rocky inclines & good eyes for keeping an eye for tripping hazards.  A fun trail with beautiful views!
Beautiful trail with tons of lookout spots along the ridge! A bit rocky in places and buggy but they mostly stayed away with a liberal application of bug spray! Definitely worth exploring!
Went early morning before 7:30AM. Absolutely beautiful & quiet. Bugs are a bit of a nuisance but other than that very few people and gorgeous views.
It's okay. Pretty short. I had to double back to satisfy my self.

Great trail, some difficult terrain near the beginning if you’re not ready for it but nothing too crazy.
Beautiful views

Great afternoon on  the Bruce Trail. Easy conditions on the Hwy 5 stretch, unfortunate few km along the road and an exciting, rough terrain and wonderful climb to the lookouts along Mount Nemo.
